req.title: Support all HTTP verbs on /status/<code>
req.statement: The system shall accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE on /status/<code>.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /status/<code> must accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE. The source shows the route is registered for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE but NOT HEAD or OPTIONS explicitly (Flask handles HEAD automatically for GET routes; OPTIONS may or may not be supported). Tests cover: (1) positive EP for each explicitly listed verb returning the exact requested status code, (2) negative path for invalid status code strings returning 400, (3) boundary values at status code edges (100, 200, 299, 300, 400, 500, 599), (4) decision table covering the comma-separated weighted random path, and (5) negative path for malformed codes. Each test uses exact status code assertions to catch comparison-operator and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_comma_separated_codes_returns_one_of_them
expected: Response status code is either 200 or 201 (weighted random path)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-017 -> comma path -> weighted_choice -> valid code returned
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_comma_separated_codes_returns_one_of_them():
    seen = set()
    for _ in range(20):
        r = client.get('/status/200,201')
        assert r.status_code in (200, 201), f'Unexpected status: {r.status_code}'
        seen.add(r.status_code)

test_comma_separated_codes_returns_one_of_them()

tests.name: test_all_verbs_accept_status_200
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each to /status/200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_verbs_accept_status_200():
    methods = [
        client.get, client.post, client.put,
        client.patch, client.delete
    ]
    for method in methods:
        r = method('/status/200')
        assert r.status_code == 200, f'{method.__name__} got {r.status_code}'

test_all_verbs_accept_status_200()
